meta.name: BMU Hub — Architecture v2 (Next Generation)
meta.status: Draft for review. Nothing is built until the owner says 'build'.
meta.builds_on: BMU Hub v12 (Dashboard Studio). Everything that works today keeps working; v2 is added in phases, each shipped as its own runnable zip.
meta.one_line_goal: Turn BMU Hub from a CRM people update into an agency operating system that runs itself: it plans the work, does the routine parts with AI, warns before things go wrong, and lets clients see and approve everything live.

what_100x_means.principle: Measured by time saved and problems caught, not by number of screens.

targets.today: People update statuses, chase approvals and write follow-ups by hand
targets.target: 80% of routine updates, reminders, follow-ups and status reports done by agents and workflows, a person only approves

targets.today: Pages load on request, refresh to see changes
targets.target: Every screen live (changes appear for everyone in under 1 second), first page load under 1.5 s, any search under 200 ms
Forecasts for revenue, capacity, churn risk and deadline slips 2–6 weeks ahead, with a suggested fix

targets.today: Clients see requests, invoices and reports
targets.target: Clients review creatives with pinned comments, approve in one tap, see live campaign results and pay online, on web and phone
Full asset library with versions, proofing, brand kits, a content calendar that publishes to social platforms and pulls back results
Quote → invoice → GST e-invoice → payment link → auto reminders → reconciled, with profit per client, project and person
Fields, forms, pipelines, workflows, roles, dashboards and client portal branding all editable without code
Mobile apps at full parity and working offline, WhatsApp as a first-class channel, public API and webhooks

baseline_v12.stack: TypeScript monorepo (pnpm). Next.js 16 web, Expo SDK 57 mobile, NestJS 12 API, Prisma 7 + PostgreSQL, packages/shared for types, validation, permissions and API client.
already_built: Lead → proposal → client journey with 5 gates
Engagements, production board, specialist and manager workspaces
Requests desk with SLAs, approvals, messages
Automations (v9), analytics and explore (v9–v10), AI copilot (v10)
Actions everywhere: add, assign, reassign, move, archive (v11)
Dashboard Studio: edit built-ins, build custom dashboards for chosen people (v12)
Audit log, role and specialty permissions, IST-aware periods
limits_to_fix: Modules call each other directly, so adding features means touching many places
No live updates: screens need refresh
Automations are simple if-this-then-that with no waiting, branching or retries
AI copilot answers questions but cannot safely take actions on its own
Search is per screen, not one search across everything
Files have no versions, proofing or library
Analytics run on live tables, so heavy reports will slow the app as data grows
Mobile needs a connection for everything
No outside integrations (ads, social, WhatsApp, payments, accounting)

architecture_principles: Modular monolith first: one API process with strict module boundaries, so it stays easy to run on one laptop; any module can be split into its own service later without rewriting.
Everything is an event: every change writes a domain event; workflows, AI agents, notifications, search, analytics and live updates all listen to events instead of being called directly.

One action system: every change (from a person, a workflow, an AI agent or the public API) goes through the same Action layer from v11, so permissions, validation, audit and undo are identical everywhere.
Shared rules: types, validation, permission policies and metric definitions live in packages/shared and are used by web, mobile, API and agents alike.
AI proposes, people approve: agents can do anything a person can, but risky actions wait for approval and every agent step is logged and reversible.

Local first for the owner: 'pnpm install' then 'pnpm dev' must keep working on Windows with only Postgres. Redis, object storage, vector search and the Python service are optional in development, with built-in fallbacks.
Light-only, minimal design matching bmumarketing.in. No dark mode.
India first: IST everywhere, INR and GST, DPDP Act 2023 compliance, data hosted in India (ap-south-1 / Mumbai) in production.

system_layers.1_experience: Next.js web (team, client, admin, creator, website), Expo mobile apps, WhatsApp, email, public API.
system_layers.2_gateway: NestJS HTTP API + WebSocket gateway, auth, rate limits, API keys.
system_layers.3_actions: Action layer (v11) extended: every write is a typed Action with policy check, validation, audit entry, domain event and undo record.
system_layers.4_domains: Sell, Clients, Deliver, Production, Service, Finance, People, Creators, Assets, Content, Knowledge, Org.
system_layers.5_platform_services: Event bus, workflow engine, agent runtime, search index, notification router, file service, metric layer, integrations hub, custom fields.
system_layers.6_data: PostgreSQL (main, with row-level security), read models, analytics schema, pgvector, object storage, Redis (cache, queues, presence).
system_layers.7_intelligence: Python service (optional, phase 7) for forecasting, anomaly detection and heavy analytics, called through the event bus.

event_bus.what: Every committed change publishes a domain event such as lead.created, engagement.phase_changed, task.overdue, invoice.paid, asset.approved.

how.outbox: Event rows are written in the same database transaction as the change (DomainEvent table), so no event is ever lost.
how.dispatcher: Background worker reads the outbox and delivers to subscribers. Uses BullMQ on Redis when available; falls back to an in-process Postgres poller (LISTEN/NOTIFY) when Redis is not running.
how.delivery: At-least-once with idempotency keys; failed deliveries retry with backoff and land in a dead-letter list visible in Admin → System health.

event_shape.correlationId: string (links a chain of events back to the first action)

event_bus.catalogue: Event types and payload schemas defined in packages/shared/src/events/ with zod, so producers and consumers can't drift.

adds: Undo: every action stores an inverse; users get a 10-second 'Undo' toast and admins can roll back any action from the audit log
Bulk actions: any action can run on a selection (up to 5,000 rows) as a background job with progress
Dry run: workflows and agents can preview what an action would change before doing it
Actor types: user, agent, workflow, api_key, system — all audited the same way
Action catalogue exposed to the command palette, workflows, AI agents and the public API from one definition

read_models.what: Fast pre-computed views (client 360 summary, team workload, pipeline totals, SLA board) updated by events instead of computed on every page load.
read_models.storage: Postgres tables prefixed rm_, rebuilt from events on demand (Admin → System → Rebuild views).

multi_tenancy.today: orgId on every row, checked in code
multi_tenancy.v2: Postgres row-level security keyed on orgId as a second safety net; per-org settings, branding, custom domain for the client portal; ready to host other agencies later (white-label) without code changes.

custom_fields_and_objects.what: Admins add fields to Leads, Clients, Engagements, Tasks, Requests, Creators, Assets; and create new record types (for example 'Shoot', 'Influencer campaign').
custom_fields_and_objects.storage: Typed JSONB column customFields per record, plus a CustomFieldDef table; indexed fields get generated columns for fast filtering.
custom_fields_and_objects.used_by: Forms, list filters, boards, dashboards, workflows, AI agents, exports, public API

form_builder.what: Drag-and-drop forms for lead capture (website), client briefs, request intake, creator onboarding, feedback surveys.
features: conditional questions
file uploads
prefill from link
spam protection
creates records through the action layer
embeddable on bmumarketing.in

core_platform.pipeline_builder: Admins edit lead stages, engagement phases, request statuses and production steps (names, order, required fields per stage, SLA per stage) instead of them being fixed in code. The existing 5 lead gates become the default template.

live_updates.how: NestJS WebSocket gateway (socket.io, Redis adapter when available). Clients subscribe to rooms (org, client, engagement, record, user). Events from the bus are pushed to the right rooms after a permission check.
live_updates.client_side: TanStack Query caches on web and mobile are patched from socket messages, so lists, boards and dashboards update without refresh.
live_updates.fallback: If the socket drops, the app polls every 20 s and shows a small 'Reconnecting' badge.

realtime_and_collaboration.presence: Avatars of who is viewing a record, 'typing' in threads, soft lock warning when two people edit the same field.

collaborative_documents.what: Briefs, proposals, scripts, meeting notes and SOPs as live documents several people edit at once.
collaborative_documents.how: Yjs (CRDT) over the WebSocket gateway, stored in Postgres; comments, mentions, version history, convert selection into a task.
collaborative_documents.editor: Tiptap rich text with blocks for tables, checklists, images, embeds of records.

realtime_and_collaboration.threads_v2: Every record has one conversation thread mixing internal notes, client messages (clearly marked), emails, WhatsApp messages and system events; mentions, reactions, read receipts, pinned decisions.

workflow_engine.what: Visual builder where admins draw a flow: when something happens → check conditions → do steps → wait → branch → ask a person → continue.
triggers: date field reached (for example 7 days before renewal)
steps: run any action from the catalogue
wait for time or until a condition
wait for approval (person or role, with escalation)
ask an AI agent (with structured output)

execution.durability: Each run is a WorkflowRun with WorkflowStep rows; state survives restarts; timers stored in the database and fired by the scheduler.
safety: dry run against real data before publishing
versioned flows (runs finish on the version they started on)
kill switch per flow and globally
execution.visibility: Run history per flow and per record ('why did this happen?') with each step's input and output.

templates: New lead: score with AI, assign by round-robin within specialty, send WhatsApp welcome, create follow-up task
Proposal sent: remind after 3 days, escalate to founder after 7
Client approved creative: move task to Scheduled, notify specialist, add to content calendar
Invoice overdue: polite reminder day 1, firm reminder day 7, call task for AM day 14, pause work flag day 30
SLA at risk: alert owner at 75% of time, manager at 100%
Renewal in 30 days: health check, AI draft of renewal proposal, meeting task for AM
Person offboarded: reassign all open work by rules from v11

ai_agent_layer.model_provider: Anthropic Claude via the official SDK, models configurable in Admin → AI (default to the latest capable model for agents and a fast model for classification). Provider wrapper so it can be swapped.

runtime.tools: Agents use the same action catalogue as people (via the action layer), plus read tools (search, record fetch, metric query). Permissions are those of the person or role the agent acts for, never more.
runtime.approval_policy: Each action marked auto (safe: drafts, tags, internal notes), confirm (needs a person: anything sent to a client, money, deletion, reassigning people) or never (agents can't do it).
runtime.memory: Per-client and per-org knowledge from documents, threads, briefs and past work, stored as embeddings in pgvector, with source links on every answer.
runtime.runs: AgentRun and AgentStep tables: every thought summary, tool call, cost and result logged; any agent change can be undone.
runtime.limits: Monthly AI budget per org and per agent, rate limits, prompt-injection guard on all outside text (emails, client messages, web pages), PII redaction where not needed.
runtime.quality: Eval sets per agent run in CI; thumbs up/down feedback from users stored and reviewed.

agents.name: Sales assistant
agents.does: Scores and enriches new leads, drafts first replies and follow-ups, books discovery calls, drafts proposals from the catalogue and past wins, flags stalled deals.

agents.name: Account manager assistant
agents.does: Weekly client status report draft, renewal and upsell suggestions, churn-risk alerts with reasons, meeting prep and meeting notes to tasks.

agents.name: Producer
agents.does: Breaks a brief into tasks with owners and deadlines based on capacity, chases overdue work, rebalances when someone is overloaded or on leave.

agents.name: Request triage
agents.does: Reads incoming client requests (portal, email, WhatsApp), classifies, sets priority and SLA, routes to the right specialist, drafts the acknowledgement.

agents.name: Finance collector
agents.does: Matches payments to invoices, drafts reminders, flags unbilled work and scope creep.

agents.name: Creative reviewer
agents.does: Checks creatives against the client brand kit (colours, logo, tone, spelling) and platform specs before they go to the client.

agents.name: Analyst
agents.does: Answers questions in plain English with charts ('which clients grew fastest this quarter?'), explains dashboard changes, writes the monthly founder report.

surfaces: copilot side panel on every screen
agent inbox: list of proposals waiting for approval with approve/edit/reject

universal_search.what: One search box (and Ctrl/Cmd+K) across leads, clients, people, tasks, requests, files, messages, documents, invoices.
universal_search.how: Postgres full-text (tsvector) plus trigram for typos, plus pgvector for meaning-based search; index kept fresh by the event bus; results filtered by the viewer's permissions.
features: filters by type, client, owner, date
recent and pinned
search inside PDFs and documents
jump to action ('reassign...', 'new task for...')

search_and_knowledge.knowledge_base: Internal wiki (SOPs, playbooks, brand guidelines per client) built on collaborative documents; AI answers cite it; client-visible articles in the portal help centre.

asset_library.what: Digital asset manager for every image, video, design file, document and logo, organised by client, campaign and tags.
asset_library.storage: S3-compatible object storage (Cloudflare R2 or AWS S3 Mumbai) with signed URLs; local disk fallback in development.
features: versions with compare side-by-side
automatic thumbnails and video previews
AI tags and search by what's in the image
usage rights and expiry for creator content
share links with expiry and password
large uploads resumable (up to 5 GB)
pin comments on an exact spot of an image or exact second of a video
draw on the frame
version-to-version comment carry-over
multi-step approval (internal → client)
approve or request changes in one tap from the portal, email or WhatsApp
approval certificate stored for disputes

creative_and_content.brand_kits: Per client: logos, colours, fonts, tone of voice, do and don't list, competitor list. Used by the creative reviewer agent and shown to specialists in their workspace.

content_calendar.what: Plan, approve, schedule and publish posts per client across platforms.
content_calendar.publishing: Instagram, Facebook (Meta Graph API), LinkedIn, YouTube, X; schedule in IST; client approval required before publish (configurable).
content_calendar.results: Pulls reach, engagement, clicks and spend back onto each post and into analytics.

creative_and_content.creator_portal_v2: Influencer and freelancer directory with rates, past performance, contracts, deliverable uploads into proofing, payouts tracked in finance.

client_portal_v2.branding: Client portal on a custom domain (for example hub.bmumarketing.in), BMU logo and colours, light-only design.
features: Live project timeline and what is waiting on the client
Proofing and one-tap approvals
Live campaign and social results with plain-English AI summary
Requests with SLA countdown and live status
Invoices, pay online (UPI, card, net banking), download GST invoices and statements
Shared files and brand kit
Meeting booking with the account manager
Monthly report (auto-generated, reviewed by AM before it is shared)
Multiple client users with their own roles (owner, approver, viewer, finance)
client_portal_v2.client_dashboard: Built on v12 Dashboard Studio; the AM picks the widgets each client sees.

finance_v2.flow: Proposal → quote → contract (e-sign) → invoice schedule → GST e-invoice → payment link → reminders → payment reconciled → revenue recognised.
features: Retainers, milestone and one-off billing; auto invoices on schedule
GST: CGST/SGST/IGST, HSN/SAC codes, e-invoicing IRN and QR via a GSP, TDS tracking
Payment links and auto-reconciliation via Razorpay (webhooks)
Expenses and vendor bills (creators, ad spend pass-through)
Time tracking (timer, timesheets, from mobile) feeding cost
Profitability per client, engagement, service and person (revenue minus time cost minus expenses)
Cash-flow forecast from invoice schedule and payment history
Export or sync to Zoho Books / Tally

people_and_capacity.capacity_planning: Each person's weekly hours, leave and holidays (India calendar); tasks carry estimates; a workload heatmap shows who is over or under booked for the next 6 weeks.
people_and_capacity.resource_booking: Drag people onto projects by week; producer agent suggests the best available specialist by skill, load and past quality.
people_and_capacity.performance: Per-person on-time rate, revisions per deliverable, client ratings, utilisation; private to the person and their managers.
people_and_capacity.hr_light: Leave requests and approval, onboarding checklists, documents, org chart (v11 tree).

metric_layer.what: Every number (MRR, pipeline value, win rate, on-time %, SLA breach %, utilisation, profit margin, NPS) defined once in packages/shared/src/metrics/ with its formula, filters and who may see it.
metric_layer.used_by: Dashboards (v12 widgets), reports, AI analyst, client portal, public API — so the same metric always shows the same number.

analytics_v2.analytics_store: Nightly and event-driven loads into an analytics schema in Postgres (star schema: facts for revenue, tasks, requests, time, posts; dimensions for client, person, service, date in IST). Heavy reports read from here, never from live tables.

forecasting.service: Python (FastAPI) service, optional, added in phase 7; reads the analytics schema; results written back as forecast tables.
models: deadline slip risk per task and project
forecasting.fallback: Simple statistical forecasts in TypeScript when the Python service is not running.

analytics_v2.anomaly_alerts: Automatic alerts when a metric moves unusually (for example a client's engagement drops 40%, or SLA breaches double).
analytics_v2.scheduled_reports: Any dashboard or report emailed or sent on WhatsApp as PDF on a schedule.
analytics_v2.goals_okrs: Company, team and person goals linked to metrics with progress shown on dashboards.

integrations_hub.model: Each integration is a connector module with OAuth connect, sync jobs, incoming webhooks and actions/triggers exposed to workflows and agents. Admin → Integrations shows status, last sync and errors.
integrations_hub.public_api: Versioned REST API (/v1) documented with OpenAPI, API keys with scopes, rate limits, generated TypeScript SDK from the shared client.
integrations_hub.webhooks_out: Subscribe external URLs to any domain event; signed payloads, retries, delivery log.
integrations_hub.zapier_make: Generic app built on the public API and webhooks.

communications.unified_inbox: Email (Gmail sync) and WhatsApp conversations linked to the right lead or client automatically; reply from the Hub; templates with variables; AI-drafted replies.

notifications_v2.router: One notification service listening to events; per-user preferences per type and channel (in-app, push, email, WhatsApp); quiet hours in IST; daily digest option.
notifications_v2.smart: Bundles related alerts, suppresses noise, raises priority for client-facing and money items.

communications.meetings: Calendar sync, booking pages, meeting records with AI notes, action items turned into tasks.

mobile_v2.parity: Everything a team member, manager or client can do on web can be done in the app, with screens designed for phones.
mobile_v2.offline_first: Local SQLite database (expo-sqlite) with a sync engine: read anything recently viewed offline, make changes offline, sync with conflict rules when back online.
mobile_specific: push notifications with quick actions (approve, reply, snooze)
camera and screen-recording upload straight into proofing
voice note to task with AI transcription
mobile_v2.release: Expo EAS builds for App Store and Play Store, over-the-air updates for fixes.

auth: Google sign-in and email magic link
passkeys and TOTP two-factor (required for Founder, Admin, Finance)

permissions_v2.model: Role- and attribute-based policy engine in packages/shared: who (role, specialty, team, client relationship) × what (record type, field) × action × condition (own, team, assigned client, amount limit).
permissions_v2.field_level: Hide or make read-only sensitive fields (rates, salaries, margins) per role.
permissions_v2.admin_ui: Permission editor with a 'view as this person' preview.

data_protection: encryption at rest (managed Postgres, object storage) and in transit (TLS)
secrets in environment/secret manager, never in code
daily backups with point-in-time restore, tested monthly
rate limiting and bot protection on public forms and login
dpdp_act_2023: consent records for leads and client users
privacy notice and purpose per data type
data export and deletion requests workflow with deadlines
data retention rules per record type

techniques: read models and caching (Redis, with in-memory fallback)
cursor pagination and virtualised lists for 100k+ rows
React Server Components and streaming on web
background jobs for anything over 1 s
database indexes reviewed from slow query log
partitioned activity, audit and event tables by month
performance_and_reliability.observability: OpenTelemetry traces and metrics, structured logs, Sentry for errors on web, mobile and API, Admin → System health page (queues, dead letters, integrations, AI spend, job failures).
performance_and_reliability.feature_flags: Per org, role or person, so new features can be switched on gradually and off instantly.

developer_and_delivery.repo: Same pnpm monorepo. New packages: packages/events, packages/metrics, packages/policies (or folders inside packages/shared), packages/ui (shared design tokens and components for web and mobile).
developer_and_delivery.local_run: Still 'pnpm install' then 'pnpm dev'. Optional 'pnpm dev:full' starts Redis, MinIO (storage) and the Python service with Docker if installed. The app detects what is running and uses fallbacks otherwise.
testing: API e2e on a fresh database (as today)
browser journeys for every flow (as today, extended per phase)
load test script for the SLO targets
developer_and_delivery.ci_cd: GitHub Actions once GitHub is connected: checks on every change, preview deploys, one-click production deploy with database migration and rollback.
developer_and_delivery.hosting_production: Docker images; API and web on a managed platform in Mumbai region; managed Postgres with replicas; Redis; R2/S3; CDN for assets.

migration_and_compatibility.rule: Each phase is additive. Existing screens, URLs, data and tests keep working; old features are switched to the new engine behind a feature flag, then the old path is removed one version later.
migration_and_compatibility.data: Prisma migrations only, never destructive in the same release that introduces a replacement; backfill jobs for events, search index and read models run on first start.
migration_and_compatibility.user_run_steps: Unchanged for every phase: unzip, cd into the folder, pnpm install, pnpm dev, open http://localhost:3000. Each zip ships with RUN_GUIDE.md.

non_goals_for_v2: Splitting into many microservices (not needed at this size; the modular design keeps the option open)
Building our own ad platform or social network features
Replacing accounting software (we sync to Zoho Books / Tally instead)

decisions_taken.decision: Modular monolith with an outbox event bus
decisions_taken.why: Gives the benefits of events (decoupling, AI and workflows listening) while staying one process the owner can run with pnpm dev.

decisions_taken.decision: Postgres for search, vectors, read models and analytics
decisions_taken.why: One database to run and back up; good enough far beyond current scale; heavy pieces can move out later.

decisions_taken.decision: Redis, object storage and Python are optional in development
decisions_taken.why: The owner runs on Windows without Docker; everything must work with only Postgres.

decisions_taken.decision: AI acts only through the action layer
decisions_taken.why: Same permissions, audit and undo as people, so AI can't do anything unsafe or untraceable.

decisions_taken.decision: Yjs for live documents, socket.io for live updates
decisions_taken.why: Proven, TypeScript-native, works on web and React Native.

decisions_taken.decision: Build order v13 → v20 as listed
decisions_taken.why: Events and live updates first because workflows, agents, search, notifications and analytics all depend on them.
